item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Antonio Senzatela (49) pitches against the Tampa Bay Rays during the eleventh inning during Game 4 of the World Series at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. on Oct 27, 2026. Jovanny Hernandez / Milwaukee Jo… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Statistically, Antonio Senzatela had one of the worst seasons as a Major League pitcher in 2025. In 30 games, 23 starts with the Colorado Rockies in the 2025 regular season, Senzatela went 4-15 with a career-worst 6.65 ERA, career-worst 22 home runs allowed, and a K: BB ratio of 73:47. Senzatela was demoted to the bullpen in late August and looked to be on the last leg of his Major League Baseball career. Oh, how things can change in a year. Antonio Senzatela Made a Remarkable Turnaround This Season Senzatela made the Rockies Opening Day roster in 2026 as a long reliever. But considering how 2025 ended, Senzatela seemed to be a few bad outings away from being out of a job. The factor going in Senzatela’s favor, though, was that he was due $12 million guaranteed in 2026 as part of the five-year, $50.5 million extension he signed with Colorado in October 2021. Fortunately for both sides, it never got to the point where difficult decisions would have to be made this season. Senzatela was lights out to begin the season. He posted eight scoreless outings in his first nine appearances of the season. With an impressive K: BB ratio of 19 Ks to just five BBs. It was the most dominant Senza had looked in years as he became one of the most reliable options out of the bullpen for the Rockies. item.title: Spirited England exit World Cup after Samoa loss
item.description: England had been bidding to reach a fifth consecutive semi-final [Getty Images] England (0) 6 Try: Cousins Goal: Rowe Samoa (12) 24 Tries: Crichton Ropati 3, Taulelei-Siala, Fanua Rimoni Goal: Piliae-Rasabale Penalty: Piliae-Rasabale England's women took one step back in the hope of taking two forward as they exited the Rugby League World Cup at the group stage. With Stuart Barrow's side defeated by Samoa - despite a spirited display - their focus immediately shifts forward to 2030. Whether that long-term strategy will bear dividends, though, is as uncertain as the location of the tournament in four years' time, which is yet to be confirmed. After reaching the semi-final stage at the previous four World Cups, England's eye was clearly on the future this time. That was reflected in Barrow's thinking for this tournament when he named a squad containing 11 players aged 23 or under. While the 70-6 rout of a Wales team ill-equipped to compete at this level on their bow had been anticipated and briefly raised expectation levels, what has followed has only underlined the gulf in class England still have to bridge. And having been humbled again by the Jillaroos just under a week ago, any suggestions that the experience was the "best preparation" they could have for a make-or-break final group game were trashed on Friday in Wollongong. Instead, the great power and pace of the Samoa players showed almost straight away. Freedom Crichton Ropati twice went over in the right corner as England fought a rearguard action and the Parramatta Eels winger completed her hat-trick before the break as Samoa enjoyed a huge territorial advantage. And it looked ominous for England when Mercedez Taulelei-Siala capitalised on a huge overload down the left to score straight after half-time and extend Samoa's lead to 16-0. However, when Evie Cousins, who had been in tears towards the end of the first period after failing to catch a routine high ball, skipped over in the left corner, after a superb line break from Hollie-Mae Dodd, it sparked England back into life. Isabel Rowe added the extras and when Pauline Piliae-Rasabale elected to take two points from a penalty for Samoa it underlined the pressure that Barrow's side had been able to apply. While England went out in the last four on a dark and dank night in York four years ago, their departure from this World Cup was in an altogether more scenic setting, with the Pacific Ocean as the backdrop. Had Fran Goldthorp been able to offload without her pass straying forward, when England had two players spare and the try-line at their mercy, it could have made for an entirely different conclusion. Instead, when they then failed to find touch after winning a penalty, they were punished ruthlessly as Fanua Rimoni crashed over for Samoa's fifth try to seal their passage into the last four and a meeting with New Zealand. item.description: Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders saves Liverpool's Ryan Gravenberch's penalty kick in the shoot out after the Carabao Cup, fourth round match at Anfield, Liverpool. Picture date: Wednesday October 28, 2026. (Photo by Peter Byrne/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images 1. MIKE PENDERS (7.1) It was a horror moment in an otherwise solid full Premier League debut for young Mike Penders over the weekend, when he punched a Spurs corner straight into the back of his own net, so it was especially great to see him put in an excellent performance in a tough environment just a couple days later. He didn’t show any obvious ill-effects, mentally or otherwise, of the gaffe; quite the contrary in fact: he made multiple good saves and a couple good punches to clear his area. Liverpool had an xG of over 2 but could only score from the penalty spot. In the shootout, Penders was nearly able to complete his redemption as he saved the effort from Ryan Gravenberch. Unfortunately, Emmanuel Emegha produced one of the worst takes of the evening when he had a chance to win it, and then Wesley Fofana one-upped that by putting his into low Earth orbit to complete our early exit from this year’s League Cup. item.title: Sophie Cunningham Says the WNBA Needs A Commissioner With “A Backbone”
item.description: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham thinks the WNBA needs a leader with a backbone, and she used a recent hour on Theo Von’s podcast to say more. In the Wednesday episode of This Past Weekend, Von’s quirky sense of humor meshed well with Cunningham’s straightforward commentary on league leadership, player salaries, rivalries, the national anthem, and her faith. Clips from the interview quickly went viral, earning plaudits from fans who appreciate her candor and those who enjoy the discourse. Cunningham, 30, is an unrestricted free agent at the end of this season after playing under a one-year, $665,000 contract. She is set to play overseas this winter as part of Project B, a brand new global women’s league, and recently launched a basketball podcast with trainer Drew Hanlen. A rocky finish and a league in transition The Fever won 28 of 44 regular-season games but fell to the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in the first round. A’ja Wilson scored 36 points as Las Vegas beat Indiana by 11 in Game 3 on Oct. 1, ending the Fever’s season for the second year in a row. When asked what the Fever lacked, Cunningham responded without hesitation: “Shots? Duh.” “We didn’t make our shots,” she said. “Just didn’t play great.” She said the loss still stings, but a few weeks at home have helped her relax. Drafted 13th overall by the Phoenix Mercury in 2019, Cunningham said the league has changed “night and day” since then. She recalled her parents downloading “some weird app” to watch her early games, only to get a black screen. She credited the 2024 rookie class, led by Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese, for bringing their college followings along with them. “If you put really any women’s sport on TV, people will fall in love with it,” she said. And the best part, she added, is that young girls now have role models who look like them and come from where they come from. ‘A backbone is needed’ Commissioner Cathy Engelbert will retire at the end of the year, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver announced on Sept. 4. Her tenure since 2019 increased team valuations, ratings, and salaries, but it has also strained the relationship with the players’ union. Cunningham gave Engelbert “a little bit of credit” for the changes, noting the league was much different when she took over. When asked if the commissioner is just retiring, Cunningham said, “I mean, that’s one way to put it.” She praised Silver as an example. “I think Adam Silver does a phenomenal job of having a relationship with his NBA players,” she said. “We need someone who has a backbone.” Cunningham said the next commissioner must keep communicating with both players and owners. “She doesn’t talk to any of us,” she said about Engelbert. “So how would we know?” Von showed a July clip of broadcaster Dan Patrick criticizing Engelbert for canceling a scheduled interview at the American Century Championship celebrity golf tournament in Lake Tahoe after waiting nearly two hours. item.title: 'Two of the greatest in history': Mike Hesson backs struggling Babar Azam, Fakhar Zaman with bold claim
item.description: Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson has backed senior batters Babar Azam and Fakhar Zaman to deliver in the ODI tri-series final against Sri Lanka on Saturday, describing the duo as two of the greatest players in the country's cricket history. Hesson believes the big occasion could bring the best out of the experienced pair, who have struggled to make an impact with the bat during the tournament. “You are talking about two of the greatest players in Pakistan’s history in the top three. I expect big players to stand up in big games," Hesson told the Pakistan Cricket Board ahead of the final at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium. However, their recent numbers have raised questions over their current form. Babar has registered scores of 45, 34, 10 and 29, while Fakhar's returns read 16, 0, 10 and 5. Despite their lack of substantial contributions, Pakistan have managed to reach the final with three successive victories. They defeated Sri Lanka by 37 runs and England by 87 runs before edging past Sri Lanka by one wicket in a thrilling encounter, where Shadab Khan's unbeaten century proved decisive. Hesson said the team's ability to win games without significant contributions from some of its established batters was an encouraging sign. He also backed them to produce a match-winning performance when it matters most. “The fact that we have been able to achieve the wins that we have without the top order performing as well as we know they are capable of is a good sign," he said. “A couple of our key players are searching for that match-winning performance, and there’s no better place to do it than in a final." Pakistan's campaign has not been without setbacks. They suffered an eight-wicket defeat to Sri Lanka in their final league fixture, but Hesson remained satisfied with the team's overall progress. He acknowledged that Pakistan had played some good cricket without putting together a complete performance and hoped they would produce their best effort in the title clash. “It’s been a pretty good couple of weeks. We have played some decent cricket without being perfect. To get three wins in a row without contributions from a few of our key players is a good sign," he said. “I still don’t think we have played our best game yet. item.description: PSG tipped to beat Liverpool in the race for midfielder Liverpool transfer latest as Aleksey Batrakov chase intensifies Liverpool are facing serious competition in the market for Aleksey Batrakov, with Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain firmly in the frame for the Galatasaray playmaker. According to TeamTalk, the 21-year-old has become one of the most closely watched young attacking midfielders in Europe, and the queue of elite clubs now reflects that status. The report states that Liverpool and Arsenal have accelerated their interest, with both clubs having scouts present when Batrakov scored in Galatasaray’s 4-2 Champions League win over Lille. That attention has built on earlier monitoring, but the wider picture is becoming increasingly crowded. Manchester United, Chelsea and Manchester City are also credited with admiration for the Russia international. What stands out most is the continental threat. “Barcelona have monitored Batrakov for some time, and the Catalan club remain in the picture.” PSG are also described as a live option, with the French champions continuing “to be regarded as a potential destination.” For any English club, that changes the dynamics quickly. Photo: IMAGO Barcelona and PSG raise pressure in Liverpool transfer plans Batrakov only joined Galatasaray in August from Lokomotiv for €25million, yet his valuation has already surged. The key detail is his release clause, with TeamTalk reporting that “his contract contains a release clause of around £50million, giving his suitors a route to negotiating a move.” In a market where attacking midfielders of this profile can command far higher fees, that figure will naturally attract attention. There is also a timing issue. Galatasaray are under no immediate pressure to sell and are said to be encouraged by his early impact. Still, “the combination of his form and the presence of a exit clause means the situation remains fluid.” That is often enough to keep major clubs engaged behind the scenes. Aleksey Batrakov profile fits elite demand Batrakov’s rise has been driven by output as much as reputation. TeamTalk notes that his “technical quality, creativity and goal threat have made him one of the most talked-about young attackers on the continent.” Those attributes help explain why Liverpool are involved, particularly as clubs continue to place a premium on versatile creators who can operate between the lines and decide matches in Europe. There is also a suggestion that personal preference could matter. “Sources believe that a move to either Barcelona or PSG would hold particular appeal, given the clubs stature and style of play.” That does not close the door on Liverpool, but it does underline the scale of the challenge. item.description: FILE PHOTO - Tottenham Hotspur's Dejan Kulusevski celebrates following the UEFA Europa League final soccer match between Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester United at the Estadio de San Mames in Bilbao. (is associated with: «Spurs star Kulusevski reveals pain behind his 526 days out injured») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Tottenham attacker Dejan Kulusevski has revealed the catalyst for his comeback after 526 days out with a knee injury. Kulusevski ended a 17-month absence with a cameo off the bench in last week’s 3-1 win over Coventry and followed it with another substitute appearance in Saturday’s victory at Chelsea. It continued a remarkable return for Kulusevski, who suffered a patella injury in his right knee in a 2-0 home defeat to Crystal Palace at the end of the 2024-25 campaign and feared his career would be over after multiple setbacks sidelined him for the entirety of last season. Ahead of facing Palace again in the Premier League on Saturday, Kulusevski told SpursPlay: “It had been like one year and a couple of months and I still can’t walk on the stairs. I can’t walk on the stairs like a normal guy. I have to play football so in my head I’m not going to give up, but I have to think that if this doesn’t work out, what do I do? “I went to a physio in Sweden. He was able to change my nervous system and then it felt different. When I did the exercises, I said, ‘I don’t have pain, like this hurt yesterday. Why is this not hurting today?’ “Then I did the next exercise and said, ‘this is not hurting,’ and I went into the room to my wife. And I told her, ‘it’s over, we’re going to do this’. From the minute I went into the room, it was better. “There was still pain but it was different. Now I had control of my leg and then that is when the grind started that summer. I started to play football and it got better every day. I was limping and everything, but it was different now.” During a wide-ranging interview, Kulusevski explained how watching Spurs celebrate Europa League glory with an open-top bus parade “was probably the most difficult part of the journey” because he could not walk to the bathroom at that stage. The former Juventus winger also revealed he initially did rehabilitation with a recommendation of old Sweden team-mate Zlatan Ibrahimovic and paid tribute to “special manager” Roberto De Zerbi. “Yeah, it’s an incredible story. I am starting to understand how to live with it, how to treat it, how to do my stretching one hour every evening before sleep and I start to understand how I can help this,” Kulusevski said. “I know I can compete and I know that because I put in the work. I am not afraid because I put in the work for one year so I know I will be ready to play and the knee is strong. “Roberto, I know from before because he is a very special manager so when he came here, it feels also like it is special. I am so happy to have him and the staff because they are different and I like to work with different people.”

item.title: Afcon to return to two-year cycle after Caf U-turn
item.description: Senegal were initial winners of Afcon 2025 before the result was overturned in favour of Morocco [Getty Images] The African Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle after a U-turn from the Confederation of African Football (Caf). In December, Caf announced that the tournament would be held every four years instead, but that decision has been reversed after a review. Under the new plans, the governing body was planning an African Nations League to replace Afcon as its biennial tournament, but acknowledged that it would take several years to generate the revenue required to become self-sufficient. "The decision by the Executive Committee to reinstate the organisation of the Afcon every two years aims to advance, protect and promote the interests of African football and the 54 Caf Member Associations, as well as those of African players playing for clubs outside the continent," Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in a statement. The biennial hosting of Afcon has long caused issues with the football calendar, with the vast majority of recent tournaments held midway through the European club season. Fifa's expanded 32-team Club World Cup was held in June and July this year, which also forced Caf to opt for mid-season dates. The next Afcon will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament, followed by editions in 2028, 2031 and 2033. There will be no tournament in 2030 because of the World Cup. The dramatic 2025 Afcon final saw Senegal crowned champions before they were stripped of their title three months later in favour of Morocco. item.title: IPL 2027: Amidst winds of change, Rohit Sharma is the glue Mumbai Indians need right now
item.description: NEW DELHI: Kieron Pollard's elevation as the new head coach and the exits of Mahela Jayawardene, Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson from the Mumbai Indians (MI) setup have already pressed the reset button in the camp. Appointments for the fielding coach and assistant coach are still pending, but the winds of change have well and truly arrived as the five-time Indian Premier League (IPL) winners look to return to their glory days. The biggest, and most crucial, piece in the puzzle, however, remains captaincy. Should they go back to Rohit Sharma? The man who led them to five titles and understands the setup better than any other player? Or should they adopt a forward-looking approach with someone like Tilak Varma? What about Jasprit Bumrah and Suryakumar Yadav? Rohit is 39 and isn't the best bet the franchise can make for the next cycle, but it's more about restoring normalcy, allowing Pollard to ease into his new role and possibly grooming the next leader in the final year of the ongoing cycle. After sweeping changes to the support staff, a sense of familiarity in the leadership group will only make the transition and preparation for future challenges smoother. Pollard and Rohit played together for several years at MI. The West Indian was part of the famous "engine room", also featuring Hardik and Krunal Pandya, that drove the franchise forward during their golden days and flourished when Rohit was at the helm. This is not to suggest that the two are the perfect recipe to restore order in that dressing room, but looking towards an inexperienced candidate at this stage will only complicate matters further. Tilak is taking giant strides in his cricketing career and is certainly the future leader of MI and Indian cricket. But right now, it's the delicate balancing act between need and want that could help the management find some answers. By no means should going back to Rohit come across as shutting the door on someone like Tilak. It's about keeping that door firmly secured until the stormy phase is well behind them and the management gains some sense of direction with the new personnel. 135350507 The 2027 edition will be more about peaceful survival and getting things right as a group before the proper reset button is pressed ahead of the mega auction. Until then, even the biggest names in the setup, barring Hardik Pandya, whose potential trade is the talk of the town, will look to coexist. A sense of familiarity will help avoid the kind of drama that followed Pandya's high-profile trade in 2023.

item.title: Jack Grealish’s absence reveals an alarming reality for Everton star
item.description: The man from No 10 was very visible. The man in the No 10 shirt was not. But then perhaps Andy Burnham is seen more at Hill Dickinson Stadium than Jack Grealish these days. As Everton advanced to the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, it was with Prime Ministerial approval and managerial disapproval of his most high-profile signing. Jack Grealish had missed a training session and so missed the 3-1 win over Newcastle, a breach of club discipline resulting in his omission. He missed out, too. The Carabao Cup may not matter much in the context of a Treble winner’s career, but it does for a club with no silverware in Grealish’s lifetime. His status and superstar’s salary can come with a responsibility. Grealish let David Moyes and Everton down. They responded by lifting themselves up. Progress came in spite of the flagship signing, not because of him. David Moyes, Manager of Everton, celebrates with Jack Grealish against Fulham last year (Getty) For Everton, with a quarter-final booked at League Two Fleetwood, with a competition opening up in the absence of Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham, Aston Villa, Manchester United, Brighton and now Newcastle, one of their best nights at their new home may make it easier to forgive. Yet their wait for a trophy is sufficiently lengthy that this could be framed of the biggest game of their season so far. And in that context, Grealish’s absence was striking. In different ways, his ill-discipline could have brought Everton’s elimination from both knockout competitions in 2026. He was suspended for January’s FA Cup exit to Sunderland after a silly sending-off. This time the ban was imposed by Everton, not the FA. “It is a club decision and I support it,” said Moyes, though he, along with chief executive Angus Kinnear, was to have been involved in the decision. Yet since Manchester City’s 2023 Champions League win, Grealish has flattered to deceive. It may be unfair to say the turning point in his footballing life was the bender in Ibiza that followed the triumph in Istanbul. It nevertheless feels accurate. Now Grealish plays too few games and scores too few goals. Whether his injury record is a consequence of his lifestyle is a matter of conjecture, but he has become a part-time presence. item.description: Tottenham Hotspur mainstay responds to Real Madrid and Barcelona links: ‘Would love to return to Spain Real Madrid’s right-back situation has been one of the most talked-about topics in recent weeks following Jose Mourinho’s tactical adjustments. The Portuguese manager has started deploying captain Federico Valverde in the position after Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold failed to convince him. Tottenham defender Pedro Porro has now addressed his future in an interview with Cadena SER’s El Larguero . Pedro Porro opens door to Spanish return The Spanish defender admitted that he would love to return to Spain while refusing to choose between Real Madrid and Barcelona. “It would be unfair to discuss anything other than my club because I have a contract. The respect they have shown me is mutual,” Porro explained. “I have always said that I would love to return to Spain because it is my country, and it would make me very excited.” Pedro Porro says he would love to return to Spain. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) The 27-year-old also addressed speculation linking him with Spain’s biggest clubs, insisting that neither had made a concrete approach. “Nobody has told me that Barcelona or Madrid want me. Clubs have asked about my situation, but there was no real interest,” he revealed. Porro extended his Tottenham contract until 2031 before the World Cup, making a potential transfer financially complicated. Would Porro suit Real Madrid better than Barcelona? When asked which club would suit his playing style better, Porro deliberately avoided taking sides. “I don’t know. I’ll let people have their opinions. I consider myself a player who can adapt to anything,” he responded. From Madrid’s perspective, Porro’s attacking qualities make him an interesting option. His overlapping runs, delivery and ability to create chances could free Valverde to return to midfield. Pedro Porro had an excellent World Cup. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Defensively, he may not be the most resolute option around, but he is definitely an upgrade on both Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold. The concern for Madrid is that any move for Porro would likely require sacrificing one of the existing right-back options in the squad. Dumfries only joined in the summer, and selling him so early might not be a feasible option for Los Blancos . That leaves the Englishman, who has struggled to get going in Spain but remains determined to prove himself under Mourinho. Porro’s desire to return to Spain is always welcome, but as things stand, Madrid might struggle to justify making this move. It remains to be seen how the right-back fares for Tottenham under Roberto de Zerbi and whether Madrid make a move for him in the future.

The Senators mounted a furious comeback, however, scoring four times in the third period to force overtime. Kings center Quinton Byfield scored in overtime to give the Kings the 6-5 victory. Hayden Hodgson Facing Possible Suspension? In 24 career NHL games, Hodgson has contributed three points, 61 hits, and 51 penalty minutes. item.description: Mumbai: Off-spinner Tanush Kotian produced a career-best 8-81 and an impressive match haul of 11-151 as Mumbai crushed Haryana by 10 wickets on the fourth and final day of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D clash at the MCA ground. The win gave Mumbai their third successive bonus-point victory of the season, marking their best start in a long time. They now have 21 points from three matches - the most among all teams in the Ranji Trophy - and sit atop their group, firmly placed on the road to the knockouts. Mumbai will next take on Railways at the Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India from November 2-5. The match will remain special for Kotian, who was playing his 50th first-class game. He marked the occasion with his first 10-wicket match haul and his fourth five-wicket haul. Chasing a modest target of 97, Mumbai openers Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Divyaansh Saxena completed the job in just 10.4 overs. Raghuvanshi, riding high after scoring his maiden first-class century in the first innings, smashed an unbeaten 67 off 39 balls. Saxena, who had struggled in his previous two innings, made a confidence-boosting 30 not out off 25 balls. The final day, however, was not entirely straightforward for Mumbai. Haryana's eighth-wicket pair of Samant Jakhar and Anuj Thakral made the hosts toil on a slow surface, adding 81 runs over nearly two hours. Kotian eventually broke the stand by bowling Jakhar. Haryana, who had resumed on 73-2, still 87 runs behind after following on, were bowled out for 256 in the second session. Reflecting on Mumbai's strong start to the season, Kotian said, "As a team, we've worked well. It's very difficult to get a third victory with a bonus point. item.description: Apr 1, 2023; Houston, TX, USA; CBS broadcaster Jim Nantz acknowledges the crowd in the semifinals of the Final Four of the 2023 NCAA Tournament between the Florida Atlantic Owls and San Diego State Aztecs at NRG Stadium. © Robert Deutsch-USA TODAY Sports CBS play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz recently grabbed headlines when a clip of him trying to peanut-punch a ball out of game analyst J.J. Watt’s hands during the Week 6 game between the Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders went viral. The playful episode showcased the growing chemistry between Nantz and Watt, who was recently permanently promoted to the post after CBS parted ways with Tony Romo. Despite the budding chemistry between Nantz and Watt, The Athletic’s Andrew Marchand remains unconvinced about the play-by-play announcer’s ability to get the best out of his analysts. Andrew Marchand Not Sold on Jim Nantz’s Effect on Lead CBS Analysts During Thursday’s segment of the “Marchand Sports Media” podcast, the analyst pinpointed the regression of Nantz’s last three partners in the booth as evidence of his claim. “Romo took the brunt of the criticism. I was one who kinda pointed out that Nantz doesn’t make his analyst better; I think that’s true,” Marchand said . “You look at Phil Simms, went backwards. You look at Tony Romo, went backwards. J.J. Watt, so far, has gone backwards. And so that’s not a great trend.” Nantz started his career as a sportscaster in the 1980s before becoming a sports anchor calling BYU Cougars and Utah Jazz games for KSL-TV. He joined CBS Sports in 1985 as a studio host for football and basketball games and as an on-course reporter for the PGA Tour. Nantz first dabbled in NFL games during Sunday Night Football matchups for CBS Radio Sports. For two seasons, he switched to college football play-by-play work and also covered the NCAA Final Four. DIVE IN: PFN’s Free NFL HQ — Team and Player Stats, Info, and More Nantz moved into play-by-play in 1988, but first called a full schedule of NFL games in 1991. He partnered with Phil Simms and became the lead play-by-play announcer for “The NFL on CBS” in 2004, after years of hosting the “NFL Today” pre-game show. In 2017, Simms was replaced by Tony Romo as Nantz’s lead color commentator. The pair called three Super Bowls together before the four-time Pro Bowler was put on leave for operating while under the influence. Nantz got another partner when Romo was eventually replaced by three-time Defensive Player of the Year, J.J. Watt, who signed a multi-year deal with CBS to continue in the role. Nantz remains part of a select club of play-by-play announcers to call both an NCAA Men’s basketball championship game and a Super Bowl, and alongside Brent Musburger, is just one of two people to ever host a Super Bowl, announce an NCAA Men’s basketball championship game, and host coverage of The Masters. item.title: Maple Leafs HC Jim Hiller Gets Backing on Sergei Bobrovsky Call
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Getty Toronto Maple Leafs fans and observers are generally passionate and tend to be brutal when judging the team based on its results. On Wednesday, October 28, the Leafs lost 5-4 to the Seattle Kraken in a game that seemed within reach, but a few costly mistakes ultimately kept them from getting back in it. The player who faced the most criticism after the loss was goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky. However, some experts believe there is room for criticism while also recognizing the situation isn’t necessarily apocalyptic. On Thursday, October 29, during Daily Faceoff’s “The Leafs Morning Take,” Nick Alberga and Jay Rosehill discussed Bobrovsky’s situation and whether he is genuinely a problem for the Leafs right now. Rosehill, in particular, took a more cautious approach. Although he criticized Bobrovsky’s performances, the former Toronto player said he still believed the goaltender could return to his best form, arguing that calls to get rid of him are exaggerated. Maple Leafs’ Bobrovsky Faces Brutal Market Reaction, per Rosehill Alberga first said, “Hey, a couple decisions were just baffling. Why do they seem so scared to go to Anthony Stolarz, and number two, any sane person watching that game would have been like, ‘you know what, let’s try to change the momentum. Let’s go with Stolarz in the third period.’ They just keep riding Sergei Bobrovsky, even though you can tell he lets in a crippling goal after crippling goal.” Rosehill said, “All you can do is support him and hopefully try to get him to play better hockey . And that’s what Jim Hiller is obviously doing . This market isn’t good at that. They don’t care. I mean, it was scrolling last night before I shut the light off. I was like, oh my God. Just all torching Bobrovsky.” “And I mean, that’s this market. There are a ton of people, and they are very passionate. And when something like this happens where there’s one clear issue at the moment, the guy gets absolutely torched. And I hope that doesn’t affect him.” “That’s what’s good about being a veteran and having all the accolades behind you: you’re probably going to be a little bit stronger to that stuff mentally. He doesn’t seem to be showing any sign of wavering in confidence. Almost to the point of pissing people off more, Hiller as well, like neglecting to acknowledge that this is bad.” “But in their mind, that doesn’t help anything. They’re going to try to do what they can to get Bobrovsky to play better hockey. And all I can do is hope that that happens. I’ve got to think that he’s got better than this, don’t you? Or is this like, like nobody knows, obviously, but the amount of people saying this ship has sailed and torch it and all the rest of it. It’s like there’s a chance he’s got better in him, right? This could be a hiccup or a bump in the road, and he’ll get more opportunities, obviously. There’s no other option.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Maple Leafs HC Jim Hiller
